<reason>B wins by explaining how inherited ownership repeatedly purchases the childhood advantages A identifies, distinguishing that durable advantage from most work-dependent high incomes. A raised substantive timing and administrative challenges, but B answered through lifetime-gift coverage, trust-pool valuation, and effects on successive generations. A nevertheless persisted with a funeral-only characterization despite B’s broader opening proposal, and misleadingly generalized B’s conditional concession about below-exemption transfers collecting nothing. B supplied the stronger comparative case without needing to claim its policy eliminates every advantage. A’s clipped second rebuttal adds a small execution cost.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B directly challenged A’s relabeling of dynastic returns as annual income: the motion compares dynastic wealth with most high earners’ income, not with every alternative capital tax. Its closing then answered “durability is not displacement” with the sharper point that an inherited asset base finances repeated displacement across generations.</best_rebuttal>
